references.text: The priests had to be consecrated before they could serve the Lord, which shows the requirement for ritual purity for those who approach God.
Describes the consecration ritual for Aaron and his sons as priests, showing how the priests were to sanctify themselves.
The Lord repeats the warning that the priests must sanctify themselves to avoid Him breaking out against them.
Nadab and Abihu were struck down by the Lord because they did not follow the holiness requirements, fulfilling the warning that the Lord would break out against them.
The priests shall be holy to their God and not profane the name of God, for they offer the Lord's fire offerings.
The Lord struck down men from Beth-Shemesh because they looked into the ark of the Lord, an example of the Lord breaking out against those who do not respect His holiness.
David commanded the Levites to sanctify themselves to carry the ark of the Lord, because the Lord had broken out against them earlier when they did not seek Him in the right way.
King Hezekiah commanded the Levites to sanctify themselves and cleanse the house of the Lord.
Our God is a consuming fire, which underscores the danger of approaching God without proper reverence and holiness.
Highlights the unique status of the priests: their access to God's presence ('coming forward') requires consecration to avoid judgment (Exodus) and justifies their special holy rights (Ezekiel).
